metadata.title: Rapport national Luxembourg — ICCS (International Civic and Citizenship Education Study) 2009
metadata.venue: ICCS (International Civic and Citizenship Education Study) — Rapport national Luxembourg

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report is based on ICCS 2009 international study data collected from students in grade 8, with additional questionnaires for teachers, school directors, and contextual information. The sampling is described at the international level as involving 38 participating countries and thousands of schools, implying a complex multistage design (students nested in schools, within countries). The national Luxembourg results are presented using the international ICCS database; however, this national report does not specify the exact weight variables (e.g., student sampling weights) or whether replicate weights were used. For analysts working with the ICCS international database, the appropriate approach is to apply the ICCS-provided student weights and to use the corresponding variance estimation method recommended by the ICCS technical documentation to obtain correct standard errors and confidence intervals under the complex survey design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report does not present a student-level predictive modeling pipeline with an explicitly documented missing-data strategy for the analysis reported here. The outcomes are reported as ICCS cognitive scale scores (Rasch-based) and questionnaire-based attitude/engagement indicators, and the document focuses on descriptive national results and curriculum-related interpretation rather than on a reproducible ML estimation procedure. As a result, the report does not provide enough methodological detail to classify a specific missing-data handling method for the reported analyses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The national Luxembourg results concern 5,019 grade-8 students from 31 schools. The report also notes that only 332 teachers out of 465 initially planned participated, and that the teacher sample did not meet the international consortium’s criteria, leading to Luxembourg being excluded from some analyses in the international report. The report does not provide further student-level inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds or complete-case criteria) for the national analyses presented here.

data.outcome_summary: This national report for Luxembourg uses ICCS 2009 data to describe students’ civic knowledge and their affective/behavioral perceptions and engagement. The cognitive test administered to grade-8 students lasted 45 minutes and included 79 items (multiple-choice and constructed-response), with items rotated across seven test booklets; a European module was also administered in Luxembourg (12-minute cognitive test plus a 17-minute questionnaire). The report reports Luxembourg’s civic knowledge mean score as 473 points (significantly below the international mean) and interprets the distribution across performance levels, highlighting a large share of students at Level 1 and below (22% below Level 1; 30% at Level 1; 19% at Level 3). For non-cognitive outcomes, it reports questionnaire-based scales with a conventional mean of 50 and SD of 10, including democratic values, gender equality attitudes, immigrant rights attitudes, trust in civic institutions, interest in political/social questions, and civic participation intentions/behaviors. It also links family context indicators (e.g., birthplace, parents’ socioeconomic status, test language, parental interest and discussion frequency) to variation in civic knowledge and interest, and discusses curriculum expectations versus implemented curriculum using document analysis and stakeholder perceptions. The report is descriptive and interpretive; it does not provide an ML model-estimation procedure or performance metrics for predictive algorithms.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a national descriptive report using ICCS 2009 results rather than an empirical ML study that trains and evaluates predictive models. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques, PV handling in a predictive sense, and main findings as ML target-variable effects are intentionally left empty because the document does not specify a supervised learning target, algorithmic pipeline, or ML performance metrics. The report does, however, provide psychometric scaling information (Rasch-based cognitive scale and questionnaire scales) and descriptive comparisons/associations, which are outside the ML-focused schema for main_findings.
